## feature

### qc-summary gained ref_len, effective_len, and efficiency columns

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Unit tests cover all three columns, including null cases, and two smoke
runs against a real BAM confirmed the values. The evidence is in this
report.

#### description

```
type: [table, text]
```

1. `ref_len` mirrors the BAM-header `LN` for every reference.
2. `effective_len` = `ref_len` − `tc_primer_start_len` − `tc_primer_end_len`.
   It is null when the reference has no TC config row.
3. `efficiency` = `on_target_rate^(1/effective_len)`. It is null when
   `effective_len` is null or ≤ 0.

Column order after the change:

| Position | Column | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | seq_name | header |
| 2 | ref_len | header LN |
| 3 | effective_len | ref_len − TC primers |
| 4–6 | total/forward/reverse reads | FLAG tally |
| 7, 9, 11 | forward_rate, fl_rate, on_target_rate | count/total |
| 12 | efficiency | on_target_rate^(1/effective_len) |
| 13–19 | ap_* buckets, error counts | AP/error tally |

#### before

The qc-summary table had no reference-length column, so consumers joined
lengths back in by hand. There was no per-base on-target metric.

#### after

One row per reference now carries the header length, the primer-trimmed
effective length, and the implied per-base on-target rate. References
without a TC config row show null, not a wrong number.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic, text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_qc_summary.py::test_qc_summary_multi_ref` asserts
  `effective_len` 12 (28−8−8), 16 (26−5−5), and null for the config-less
  reference, plus `efficiency == 0.5**(1/12)`.
- Smoke run (real CLI, 10 bp ref, tc primers 2+3): `effective_len == 5`,
  `efficiency == 0.870551 == 0.5**(1/5)`.

:::

### error-stats emits a per-reference ref_summary parquet

```
level: high
```

#### reason

A unit test pins both metrics against hand-derived depth arrays, checks
the zero-read and partial-coverage cases, and asserts value parity with
`error.parquet`'s rate columns. The full suite passes.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. New 8th output `{p}.ref_summary.parquet` (`--ref-summary-out`).
2. `max_min_rate` = min depth / max depth over all reference positions,
   on the same depth universe as `error.parquet`'s `total`. A zero-depth
   base pins it at 0.0. No reads also gives 0.0.
3. `max_error_rate` = max over positions of max(insertion_rate,
   deletion_rate, mismatch_rate). It equals the worst per-position rate
   in `error.parquet`.
4. `--prefix` now writes 8 files; explicit form requires all 8
   `--*-out` paths.

#### before

Depth evenness and the worst positional error rate had to be derived by
re-aggregating `error.parquet` downstream, one position at a time.

#### after

One row per reference answers both questions directly. The value
convention matches the existing rate columns, so the two sources agree
by construction.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_stats.py::test_ref_summary_max_min_and_max_error_rate`:
  depth `[4,3,3]` → `max_min_rate 0.75`, `max_error_rate 1/3`; zero-read
  ref → `(0.0, 0.0)`; partial-coverage ref (depth `[1,1,0]`) →
  `max_min_rate 0.0`; parity check against `error.parquet` rows.
- Smoke run (uniform depth 2, one mismatch): `max_min_rate 1.0`,
  `max_error_rate 0.5`, matching the `error.parquet` row
  (`mismatch 1, total 2, mismatch_rate 0.5`).

:::

### subcommand help lists the output columns

```
level: high
```

#### reason

All three help screens were captured verbatim after the change and render
as intended.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `error-stats --help` shows a markdown table of all 8 outputs and their
   columns.
2. `qc-summary --help` lists every column plus the `effective_len` and
   `efficiency` formulas.
3. `pileup --help` states its column list; `--output` help points there.

#### before

The help named the output files but not their columns. Users opened the
docs to learn the schema.

#### after

The schema is visible at the point of invocation. The error-stats table
renders correctly because cyclopts auto-detects markdown tables.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `sam-tagger error-stats --help` output shows the 8-row table with
  aligned columns (captured this session).
- `sam-tagger qc-summary --help` lists all 20 columns and both formulas.

:::

## fix

### usage.qmd error-stats output table was split by interleaved prose

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The defect was visible in the source (table rows separated by three
prose paragraphs) and the repaired table is in the committed file.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The `error` row sat above three paragraphs; the other six rows
   followed below. Markdown rendered this as one 1-row table plus an
   orphaned fragment.
2. The table is now one 8-row block, followed by the prose.

#### before

Readers saw a broken table: one row, then prose, then stray rows that
did not render as a table.

#### after

The full output table renders as one block, now with the eighth output.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/usage.qmd` lines 159–171 (before): row `error` at line 161,
  remaining rows at 195–200, prose between.
- After: single table `error` … `ref_summary`, then the prose paragraphs.

:::

## limitation

### ref_summary depth metrics follow sam-tagger's own read universe

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The depth semantics are inherited from `error.parquet`'s `total` column
and are documented there, but the exact samtools-equivalence conditions
were verified for `total`, not re-verified for `ref_summary` this session.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `max_min_rate` uses all mapped cs-carrying reads. It is not
   region-gated.
2. It equals a samtools-derived rate only under the conditions documented
   for `error.parquet`'s `total` (no secondary/QC-fail/duplicate records,
   every mapped read carries `cs`).

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py`, `_write_ref_summary_stats`
  docstring and `_depth_array` reuse.
- `docs/usage.qmd` "error-stats" section, `total` paragraph.

:::

## caveat

### _pct → _rate is a breaking rename for qc-summary consumers

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The rename changes output column names that downstream code reads by
name; the wps_1012 workflow is a known consumer.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `forward_pct`, `fl_pct`, and `on_target_pct` no longer exist. Use
   `forward_rate`, `fl_rate`, `on_target_rate`.
2. The values did not change. They were already 0–1 fractions.
3. The release notes carry the mapping verbatim.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Release notes `v0.6.0`, "Breaking changes" section (installed via
  `gh release edit` this session).
- Commit `3f5816c` `feat!: rename qc-summary _pct columns to _rate...`.

:::

## assumption

### max_min_rate counts zero-depth positions in the minimum

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The user's example `[3,1,4,5] → 1/5` does not distinguish the two
readings. The literal reading was implemented and stated in the reply;
the user has not yet confirmed it.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Interpretation: min and max run over ALL reference positions, zeros
   included. One uncovered base yields `max_min_rate = 0.0`.
2. If the intent was "minimum over covered positions only", the change
   is one line in `_write_ref_summary_stats`.

## observation

### cyclopts renders markdown tables in help without a help_format setting

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

A two-app probe (default vs `help_format="markdown"`) produced identical
table rendering; plain indented text collapsed its line breaks.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Default help rendering collapses single newlines in docstrings.
2. Markdown tables render as tables in both modes.
3. The docstrings therefore use a markdown table instead of an indented
   block.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Probe run this session: `plain` and `md` apps both rendered the
  2-row table identically.

:::

## process

### reset the pre-addition bump commit and tag before the mid-task asks

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The version bump and `v0.6.0` tag were cut before the user's mid-task
   additions (help readability, effective_len, efficiency) arrived.
2. Because nothing was pushed, the tag was deleted and the bump commit
   reset locally, the additions landed as their own commits, then the
   bump and tag were re-cut.
3. This kept the release content complete and the history one-change-per-
   commit.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `git log --oneline -6` shows `3f5816c`, `742dc40`, `de18899`,
  `98a3ec4`, `7ceb952`, `f053f8e` — each a single logical change, tag on
  the last.

:::

### hand-derived depth array in the first ref_summary test was wrong

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first version of the ref_summary test asserted depths from a
   hand-computed array that ignored coverage from two cs ops.
2. The implementation was correct; the test expectations were not
   (observed `0.75, 1/3` vs asserted `0.25, 1.0`).
3. The better action: recompute the depth array from the difference-array
   semantics op by op before writing expectations. Done; the corrected
   test passes.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Failure output: `assert (0.75, 0.3333...) == (0.25 ± …, 1.0 ± …)`.

:::
